text.p: Alien abductions, government plots, phantom 1959 Cadillacs prowling rural roads. Elvis, where are you?

Two decades after his death there are some who still believe Elvis Presley is not buried in the Meditation Garden at Graceland Mansion in Memphis -- or anywhere else. Those who refuse to accept his death prefer to believe the "King of Rock 'n' Roll" is still around at age 62, caught in a trap of his own or another's making.

"I saw Elvis the other day at a local Mobil Mart. When I left the building there was a large UFO hovering above the store. Elvis walked out, winked at me and then said 'Want some pork rinds?' I watched as he was beamed up to the spacecraft," said an entry on one of many Presley sites on the Internet that are crackling with new life as the 20th anniversary of his death, on Aug. 16, 1977, approaches.

"Elvis was not a real person. He was dreamed up by our government to stimulate growth in the economy. The actors who played the part of Elvis started asking for too much money and the government cancelled the project. Elvis sightings are a result of someone recognising one of the former actors," says an entry on www.elvissightings.com/elvis/index.html. The Web site is ripe with irreverence, scepticism and humour in addition to the views of obvious true believers.

The American penchant for accepting conspiracy theories, a parade of supermarket tabloid stories -- "FBI to Dig Up Elvis' Grave ... rumours he's alive too strong to ignore" -- and perhaps plain wishful thinking have kept the stories alive.

"On May 13, 1994, I was driving by myself just outside Durham, North Carolina, when my car started bucking. I pulled off the road in a rather remote area. I was working under the hood ... when a 1959 Cadillac sedan with tinted windows pulled alongside me," said an entry on the site.

"The driver asked if he could be of any assistance. ... As the Cadillac pulled away I noticed through the back window that was down three or four inches, seated in the back seat of the car was Elvis Presley. He was wearing sunglasses and had a slight grin on his face ..."

One entry had another explanation for the Elvis conspiracy: "Few people know that Elvis was in fact a government (drug) agent by special appointment from the president of the United States. ... I believe that the government helped Elvis fake his own death and be placed in a witness protection plan to protect his family and close friends ..."

Vernon Chadwick, the self-styled world's "greatest living Elvis expert," has organised a six-day conference on Elvis at the Memphis College of Art that will conclude on Saturday, the 20th anniversary of Presley's death at the age of 42 of a drug-induced heart attack.
The conference will feature, among other things, a presentation on Elvis's influence on Mariachi music and the first scholarly paper ever to require a karaoke machine.
Chadwick's explanation for Presley's life after death?

"The sighting of a hero, martyr or religious figure is a perennial theme. I don't mean to be blasphemous but perhaps the first Elvis sighting was Jesus Christ after the resurrection. It's not a unique event in human history," he said. "Heroes and mythic figures continue to be sighted after their deaths because they live on in our imagination. These are just the continued American versions of ancient themes."
